rationale: The Latin anchors falx (sickle/scythe), marra (hoe/mattock), falcastrum (pruning hook), and ensis curvus (curved sword) all denote bladed or cutting implements, firmly anchoring BIL to the sharp cutting edge of a blade. The Beowulf attestations confirm a sword/blade sense, making edge.n.03 ("a sharp side formed by the intersection of two surfaces of an object") the correct synset over the more general boundary or perimeter senses.
